data.body:
CONCURRENT-WORK COLLISION — read before implementing the current plan. Not resolving this unilaterally; flagging it for the operator.

WHAT LANDED. A change implementing this ticket is ALREADY MERGED on origin/main as c68cc1de3185 ("Resolve the sweep's code root, not compose it", Gerrit 2344, submitted by JoeOakhartNava at 22:56). It carries LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1 (CI run 33216372220 SUCCESS) and the rebar-ticket: 6bf1-326b-7404-4034 trailer. It implements run_sweep as the BARE `config.repo_root_or_none()`, removes the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction (guard allowlist now holds zero deferred config-root sites), and adds four tests to tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py plus the guard self-test.

WHAT THE DESCRIPTION NOW SAYS. The description has since been rewritten to mandate a DIFFERENT design — a dedicated `compaction_child_repo_root(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)` with precedence REBAR_ROOT-realpath > dirname(canonical tracker) — and AC#1 explicitly excludes "`repo_root_or_none()` git-toplevel arm". That symbol does not exist anywhere in origin/main. So the current ACs describe work that is NOT what landed, which is why the close gate reports every box unchecked: I will not tick boxes for an implementation that is not in the tree, and per policy I will not --force.

THE DESIGN DISAGREEMENT, STATED FAIRLY. The rationale comment above is right that `repo_root_or_none()`'s non-REBAR_ROOT arm reads git-toplevel-of-CWD, so the merged implementation's local-topology correctness DEPENDS on `_proc.detached_child_cwd` continuing to anchor the child at dirname(realpath(tracker)). That is a real non-local coupling, and the merged code documents it explicitly rather than hiding it. It also applies unevenly: run_sweep has a SYNCHRONOUS caller too (maybe_compact when compact.trigger == "always"), where no anchoring applies and the cwd is simply the caller's.

But the proposed replacement is not strictly better, and the tradeoff should be made with eyes open: its fallback arm, `dirname(canonical tracker)`, IS "compose the config root from the store path" — the exact construct this ticket's whole class exists to eliminate and that scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py flags. It is correct only while REBAR_ROOT is set on every relocated store; a relocated store with REBAR_ROOT unset gets the store's parent, i.e. the original bug. So one design leans on cwd anchoring, the other leans on REBAR_ROOT always being exported. Both are defensible; neither is free.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION (operator decision, not mine).
(a) If the merged design is accepted: revert the description's AC block to describe what landed, tick the boxes, and close. No code change needed.
(b) If the dedicated resolver is preferred: keep this ticket open and land it as a follow-up REFACTOR on top of c68cc1de3185 — not as a from-scratch implementation, since the sanction is already drained and the tests already exist. Note that a `dirname(canonical tracker)` fallback will need its own `# repo-root-ok:` sanction or it re-populates the guard allowlist this ticket's AC#3 just emptied, which is worth deciding deliberately.

Either way the defect itself is FIXED on main today; what remains is which resolver shape the project wants.
